# The Local Answer Gap: what 7,583 Google AI answers reveal about AEO for local businesses

By the [Local AI Registry Research Team](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap#authors)

The short answer

Local AI Registry’s analysis of 7,583 Google AI Overviews shows that when people ask AI about a local business, the business rarely supplies the answer. In 207 AI answers about local businesses, news outlets supplied two-thirds of the citations and the businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%. The AI usually answered with chain-wide facts and told people to check with their local store. Answer engine optimization (AEO) closes that gap.

- **55,393** Google searches
- **7,583** AI Overview answers
- **98,020** fact-checked claims
- **1,496** cited pages read
- **29** original charts and explainers

## Key findings

1. Local AI Registry found that local business searches triggered a Google AI Overview 76.4% of the time, the highest of any topic and over five times the 13.7% average (US searches, March to April 2026).
2. In Local AI Registry’s analysis, news outlets supplied 67.5% of citations in Google’s AI answers about local businesses, and Gannett newspapers alone appeared in 90.3% of those answers.
3. Businesses’ own websites supplied only 6.5% of citations in local AI answers, and directories such as Yelp, MapQuest and OpenTable supplied 0.5%, according to Local AI Registry.
4. Local AI Registry found that brand websites ranked on Google’s first page in 147 of 157 brand questions but were cited by Google’s AI in only 70.
5. 83.6% of local AI answers told people to check with their local store, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number, Local AI Registry found.
6. When Google’s AI attributed a local fact to a store locator, app or official site, 51.6% of those claims were not supported by any page it cited, according to Local AI Registry.
7. Cited social media posts had a median of 8 readable words, and 78% were too thin for AI to verify anything, in Local AI Registry’s review of 1,496 cited pages.
8. Asking the same local question in different words changed about two-thirds of the sources Google’s AI cited, Local AI Registry found.
9. Only 2 of 39,676 queries in public AI search research datasets ask an AI to find a local service provider, according to Local AI Registry’s census.

## What is AEO, and how is it different from SEO?

Search engine optimization (SEO) gets a business into a list of blue links. Answer engine optimization (AEO), also called generative engine optimization (GEO), gets a business into the answer itself: the paragraph that Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity or Microsoft Copilot writes before anyone clicks. To write that paragraph, the AI pieces together facts from sources across the internet. If it can’t find clear, consistent facts about a business, it guesses, hedges or leaves the business out.

Local AI Registry is a local AEO company. It builds a verified public record for each local business, has the owner confirm it, and pushes those facts to the places AI reads. This study asks a simple question: when AI answers a local question today, where do its facts come from, and what should a local business do about it?

![Illustration comparing a search results page of blue links (SEO) with an AI answer box that cites a few sources (AEO)](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

**Illustration 1. SEO gets you into the list. AEO gets you into the answer.** Search engine optimization (SEO) earns a place in a list of links. Answer engine optimization (AEO) earns a place inside the AI-written answer that appears before any links. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/seo-vs-aeo-explained-illustration.png)

Answer engine optimization (AEO)
:   Making a business’s facts clear, consistent and machine-readable so AI systems include it accurately in their answers.

Generative engine optimization (GEO)
:   The academic term for optimizing content to be cited by generative AI search engines; used interchangeably with AEO.

Google AI Overview
:   The AI-written answer Google shows above search results for many queries, with links to the sources it cited.

Citation
:   A source link the AI attaches to its answer. Being cited is how a business’s own pages shape what AI says.

Local intent
:   A search about a physical place: hours, location, services, availability, or finding a provider nearby.

AI visibility
:   How often, how prominently and how accurately a business is named in AI answers, measured as a rate across many answers to the same question.

Google Business Profile
:   Google’s free business listing, which holds a location’s hours, address, services and reviews, and which Google’s AI appears to draw on for store-level facts.

LocalBusiness structured data
:   Schema.org markup on a website that states a business’s name, address, hours and services in a format machines read directly.

## Is anyone studying how AI answers local questions?

Almost no one. Across 39,676 unique queries in four public AI-search research datasets, 239 concern a physical business and only 2 ask an AI to find a local service provider.

![Table of four public AI search datasets: 39,676 unique queries, 239 about physical businesses, 2 asking for a local provider](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.png)

**Figure 1. Only 2 of 39,676 public AI-search research queries ask AI to find a local provider.** Across four public AI-search datasets, 239 of 39,676 unique queries (0.6%) concern a physical business, and only 2 ask an AI to find a local service provider. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/public-ai-search-datasets-local-query-census.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Dataset | Unique queries | About a physical business | Ask for a local provider |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| IMC 2026 Google AI Overviews | 32,608 | 237 | 0 |
| Organikpi, 13 public datasets | 7,045 | 2 | 2 |
| Cited.io, Oct 2026 | 23 | 0 | 0 |
| Total | 39,676 | 239 | 2 |

Every public dataset we found studies informational, software or news queries. The only local questions with real AI answers attached are national chains’ holiday hours, so that is where we looked. It is a clean test: a simple, verifiable fact about a physical place. It also means most AEO advice for local businesses rests on very little local evidence.

## How we did this research

We re-analyzed the raw records released with Measuring Google AI Overviews: Activation, Source Quality, Claim Fidelity, and Publisher Impact (Xu, Iqbal and Montgomery, IMC 2026). The dataset covers 55,393 trending Google searches in the United States from March 13 to April 21, 2026, including 7,583 AI Overviews, every cited link, the page-one results shown beside each answer, the saved text of cited pages, and fact-check verdicts for 98,020 claims.

- **Local filter.** We tagged searches about a physical business’s hours, open status, closures or “near me,” then read every match by hand. That produced 271 local searches, 207 AI answers and 189 unique questions.
- **Comparison group.** The other 7,376 AI answers in the dataset.
- **Source groups.** Every cited domain was sorted into owner groups, including Gannett newspapers (31 domains) and TEGNA TV stations (13 domains), using their published lists of owned outlets.
- **Replication check.** Our extraction found the same 7,583 AI Overviews the paper reports, and our overall unsupported-claim rate (11.03%) matches its published 11.0%.

![Bar chart of local business searches by collection day in March and April 2026, peaking at 185 on April 6](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-business-searches-by-day-easter-2026.png)

**Figure 2. Local “is it open” searches spiked the day after Easter.** 185 of 271 local searches in the dataset were collected on April 6, 2026, the day after Easter, which is why most local answers in this study are about holiday hours. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-business-searches-by-day-easter-2026.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-business-searches-by-day-easter-2026.png)

## How often does Google’s AI answer local business questions?

More often than any other topic: 76.4% of local business searches showed a Google AI Overview, against 13.7% of all searches.

![Bar chart of AI Overview activation by category: local business 76.4%, science 39.9%, all others lower](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**Figure 3. Local business searches trigger Google AI Overviews more than any other topic.** 76.4% of local-business searches showed a Google AI Overview, nearly double the next category (science, 39.9%) and over five times the 13.7% average. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/google-ai-overview-activation-by-search-category.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Category | AI Overview shown | Searches | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local business (our filter) | 207 | 271 | 76.4% |
| Science | 622 | 1560 | 39.9% |
| Hobbies | 372 | 981 | 37.9% |
| Health | 74 | 278 | 26.6% |
| Business & finance | 875 | 3341 | 26.2% |
| Food & drink | 50 | 258 | 19.4% |
| Technology | 86 | 464 | 18.5% |
| Jobs & education | 43 | 252 | 17.1% |

| Shopping | 22 | 155 | 14.2% |
| Autos | 19 | 136 | 14.0% |
| Other | 399 | 2949 | 13.5% |
| Pets | 6 | 45 | 13.3% |

| Beauty & fashion | 5 | 142 | 3.5% |

![Bar chart: local searches 76.4%, other question searches 64.1%, all searches 13.7% showed an AI Overview](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png)

**Figure 4. Local searches got an AI answer 76% of the time, even more often than other questions.** Controlling for phrasing, local searches were still 12 points more likely to get an AI Overview than other question-style searches (76.4% vs 64.1%). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-search-ai-overview-rate-vs-question-searches.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Group | AI Overview shown | Searches | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local business searches | 207 | 271 | 76.4% |
| Other question-style searches | 2445 | 3812 | 64.1% |
| All searches | 7583 | 55393 | 13.7% |

Part of the gap is phrasing, because local searches are usually questions and questions trigger AI answers more often. Even against other question-style searches (64.1%), local searches were 12 points more likely to get an AI answer. When someone asks about a place, Google’s AI is the first thing they read.

AEO takeaway

For local questions, the AI answer is now the front door.

### What to do

Find out what AI says about your business today, for the questions customers actually ask: hours, services, prices and “best near me.”

### How Local AI Registry does it

Every business gets a public record on Local AI Registry showing what AI currently says about it, and owners can run a free AI visibility audit to see where answers are wrong or missing.

## Where does Google’s AI get its facts about local businesses?

From the news, not the business. News outlets supplied 67.5% of citations in local answers; businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5%.

![Diagram: a local question goes to Google’s AI, which pulls mostly from news outlets, then social posts, portals and rarely the store’s own site, and returns an answer that tells you to check your store](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

**Illustration 2. How Google’s AI builds an answer about a local business.** For local questions, Google’s AI assembled answers mostly from news coverage (67.5% of citations), rarely from the business itself (6.5%), and usually ended by telling people to check with their local store. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-google-ai-builds-a-local-answer-illustration.png)

![Heatmap of cited source types: Gannett newspapers 28.3% of local citations and cited in 90.3% of local answers; business’s own site 6.5%](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap.png)

**Figure 5. Who Google’s AI cites for local business questions vs everything else.** In local answers, Gannett newspapers supplied 28.3% of citations and appeared in 90.3% of answers. Businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5% of citations. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/who-google-ai-cites-for-local-business-questions-heatmap.png)

USA Today and its network of local papers (IndyStar, Delaware Online, North Jersey, El Paso Times and dozens more) publish “what’s open” roundups every holiday, and TEGNA’s local TV stations do the same. Google’s AI treats those roundups as the record. Directories barely register: Yelp, MapQuest and OpenTable together supplied 8 of 1,497 local citations.

![Bar chart of how over-represented each source type is in local answers: TEGNA 18x, portals 4.1x, Gannett 3.9x, other news 1.8x, own site 1.3x, social 0.7x](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/local-news-overrepresented-in-ai-local-answers.png)

**Figure 7. TEGNA TV stations are 18 times more likely to be cited in local answers than in other answers.** Relative to other topics, local answers lean on TEGNA TV stations 18 times more, AOL/Yahoo/MSN 4.1 times and Gannett 3.9 times. Social media is used less (0.7 times). **Figure 9. The vaguer the local question, the less the business gets cited.** Businesses’ own sites made up 8.8 to 10.9% of citations when a brand was named, but only 1.0% for generic “what’s open” questions, which is how people discover new places. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citation-sources-by-local-question-type-heatmap.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| “Is Target open?” | 123 | 8.8% | 25.0% | 7.2% | 31.5% | 9.3% | 12.2% | 6.0% |
| “Target Easter hours” | 29 | 10.9% | 29.3% | 3.3% | 35.9% | 4.9% | 7.1% | 8.7% |
| “What’s open today?” | 43 | 1.0% | 29.6% | 8.9% | 33.9% | 7.7% | 8.9% | 10.1% |
| Banks, post offices | 12 | 2.2% | 49.5% | 7.5% | 20.4% | 7.5% | 4.3% | 8.6% |

The vaguer the question, the less the business is cited. For “what’s open today” questions, which is how people discover new places, businesses’ own sites supplied 1.0% of citations. For an independent business that no newspaper writes about, there is no roundup to cite.

AEO takeaway

AI trusts what others publish about you more than what you publish yourself.

### What to do

Get your facts into third-party sources AI already reads: local news, press releases and community roundups. Earned coverage is the citation layer for local answers.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Press releases and media distribution put a business’s confirmed facts on news sites, and the Local AI Registry record itself is an independent third-party source AI can cite.

## Does ranking on Google mean AI will use your website?

No. Brand websites ranked on page one in 147 of 157 brand questions, but the AI cited them in only 70.

![Illustration of a store website ranking at the top of Google page one while the AI answer next to it cites news sites instead](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.png)

**Illustration 3. Ranked first, still skipped: why SEO alone isn’t AEO.** In 147 of 157 brand questions the store’s own site ranked on page one, but the AI cited it in only 70. Ranking and being used by AI are separate outcomes. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ranked-vs-used-by-ai-illustration.png)

Walmart ranked in 11 of 15 answers and was cited once. | Publix | 100% | 22% | 31% | 6% | 26% | 8% | 4% |
| Trader Joe’s | 100% | 26% | 20% | 3% | 28% | 5% | 3% |
| Starbucks | 0% | 0% | 14% | 0% | 51% | 24% | 0% |
| Dunkin’ | 50% | 7% | 21% | 0% | 38% | 10% | 24% |
| Aldi | 83% | 13% | 28% | 6% | 17% | 2% | 13% |
| Lowe’s | 83% | 16% | 16% | 0% | 45% | 3% | 19% |
| Sam’s Club | 100% | 20% | 30% | 15% | 15% | 5% | 15% |
| Post office | 25% | 3% | 61% | 10% | 13% | 6% | 3% |
| Chipotle | 0% | 0% | 42% | 0% | 10% | 26% | 10% |
| No brand named | n/a | 1% | 30% | 9% | 33% | 8% | 9% |

Walmart, the most-asked brand, ranked on page one in 11 of 15 answers and was cited once. Starbucks and Chipotle were never cited for their own hours. Publix, Trader Joe’s, Sam’s Club, Kroger and Home Depot were cited every time. Ranking still matters: only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside page one, while the AI went past page one for 48.8% of portal citations and 39.8% of TEGNA citations.

![Bar chart of the share of each source type’s citations that came from outside Google’s first page; business sites 4.1%, portals 48.8%](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source.png)

**Figure 13. The AI goes past page one for news, not for business websites.** Only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside Google’s first page, versus 48.8% for AOL/Yahoo/MSN and 39.8% for TEGNA stations. A business site has to rank to be used. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-citations-from-outside-google-page-one-by-source.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Source type | Citations from outside page one |
| --- | --- |
| AOL, Yahoo, MSN | 48.8% |
| Everything else | 47.4% |
| TEGNA TV stations | 39.8% |
| Other news | 28.0% |
| Gannett newspapers | 18.4% |
| Social media | 6.6% |
| Business’s own site | 4.1% |

AEO takeaway

SEO gets you ranked. AEO gets you used.

### What to do

Write pages that answer one question each in plain sentences, such as “Are you open on Easter?” or “What do you charge for Botox?” Put the answer in the first line, then the details.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s AEO content work builds question-and-answer pages, topical maps and structured data on the client’s own site, so the page that ranks is also the page AI can quote.

## Why does Google’s AI tell people to “check with your local store”?

Because it answers local questions with national facts. 83.6% of local answers hedged, and only 1 of 207 named an address.

![Waffle chart of 207 squares, 173 highlighted for answers that hedged with check locally or call ahead](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.png)

**Figure 14. 173 of 207 local AI answers told people to check with their local store.** 83.6% of local AI answers sent the reader back to the store (“check your local store,” “call ahead,” “hours may vary”), against 2.6% of other answers. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answers-telling-people-to-check-local-store-waffle.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Group | Hedged |
| --- | --- |
| Local answers | 83.6% |
| Other answers | 2.6% |

![Grouped bar chart: 83.6% of local answers hedge, 65.7% frame the answer at chain level, 0.5% give an address](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png)

**Figure 15. AI answers local questions with national facts.** 65.7% of local answers spoke about “all locations” or “most stores” (vs 2.3% of other answers), and 83.6% hedged (vs 2.6%). National facts are the AI’s default for local questions. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/how-ai-answers-local-questions-national-framing.png)

| Measure | Local answers | Other answers |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tells you to check locally | 83.6% | 2.6% |
| Answers at chain level | 65.7% | 2.3% |
| Gives address or phone | 0.5% | 0.8% |

![Waffle chart of 207 squares with a single highlighted square for the one answer that gave an address or phone number](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

**Figure 16. 1 of 207 local AI answers named a street address or phone number.** Only 1 of 207 local AI answers gave a street address or phone number. The AI answered about chains, not places. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-local-answers-with-address-or-phone-waffle.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Answers | With address or phone |
| --- | --- |
| 207 | 1 |

The AI knows its answer is not about your location, so it hands the question back to the reader. Whoever publishes location-level facts in a form AI can read gets to answer instead of a hedge.

AEO takeaway

Location-level facts are the gap. Fill it and you replace the hedge.

### What to do

Publish your own hours, holiday hours, address, services and prices for your exact location, in plain text and in LocalBusiness structured data, and keep your Google Business Profile current.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Owners claim their Local AI Registry record for free and confirm each fact. Local AI Registry manages the Google Business Profile, adds LocalBusiness structured data that links back to the verified record, and keeps holiday hours current.

## Can Google’s AI actually read your website?

Often not. When the AI said “the store locator says,” 51.6% of those claims were not supported by any page it cited.

![Bar chart: 51.6% of local claims quoting a store locator or app were unsupported, vs 6.7% of other local claims](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.png)

**Figure 17. When Google’s AI says “the store locator says,” half the time it can’t show it.** 16 of 31 local claims that cited a store locator, app or official site (51.6%) were not supported by any page the AI cited, against 6.7% of other local claims. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-store-locator-claims-unsupported-rate.png)

**Data behind this chart:**

| Claim type | Unsupported | Total | Rate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local claims quoting a store locator, app or official site | 16 | 31 | 51.6% |
| All other local claims | 148 | 2,222 | 6.7% |
| Non-local claims quoting an official source | 49 | 465 | 10.5% |

Examples written by the AI and not found in its sources include “The Aldi store locator indicates Easter Sunday: Closed” and “Target Store Locator lists Easter Sunday as closed.” The pattern suggests the AI gets store-level hours from somewhere it does not cite, likely Google’s own business listing data, and attributes them to a locator page it could not read.

![Illustration of three page types: a news article full of readable text, a store locator page made mostly of scripts, and a social post with a photo and a few words](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

**Illustration 4. What Google’s AI can actually read on a page.** News pages the AI cited had about 500 readable words. Store locator pages were mostly scripts, and the median cited social post had 8 readable words. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/what-ai-can-read-on-a-web-page-illustration.png)

![Two by two of source types by how often they were cited and how often their pages had readable text; social is cited but 78% unreadable](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

**Figure 18. Cited vs readable: what Google’s AI could actually read.** News pages were both cited and readable. Social posts were cited in 48% of local answers but 78% were thin (median 8 words). 11% of businesses’ own pages were thin. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/cited-vs-readable-ai-sources-2x2.png)

| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |

| TEGNA TV stations | 41.5% | 108 | 514 | 0.0% |
| Other news | 92.3% | 479 | 499 | 0.2% |
| AOL, Yahoo, MSN | 43.0% | 123 | 639 | 0.0% |

Store locator pages were also thin: Trader Joe’s store search had 97 words and Cracker Barrel’s Easter page 18. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/readable-words-on-ai-cited-pages-by-source.png)

| --- | --- |
| AOL, Yahoo, MSN | 639 |
| Everything else | 569 |
| TEGNA TV stations | 514 |
| Other news | 499 |
| Gannett newspapers | 453 |
| Business’s own site | 350 |
| Social media | 8 |

AEO takeaway

If AI can’t read it, it can’t cite it, and it may misquote it.

### What to do

Keep key facts in plain HTML text, not inside store-locator scripts, images or social posts. A one-page “hours and holidays” page beats a widget. Post updates on your website as well as on Instagram or Facebook.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s technical AEO work makes sites readable to AI crawlers: text versions of key facts, schema markup, an llms.txt file, and readable descriptions on photos and media.

## Do AI answers about local businesses stay the same?

The verdict does; the sources don’t. Different wording of the same question changed about two-thirds of the cited sources.

![Illustration of three phrasings of the same Target question, each citing a different mix of websites, all producing the same closed verdict](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

**Illustration 5. Different wording, different sources, same answer.** Three ways of asking about Target on Easter returned the same verdict but shared only about a third of their sources. No single publisher owns a local answer. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-sources-rotate-same-verdict-illustration.png)

![Bar chart of source overlap: 35% shared for the same brand asked in different words on the same day](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

**Figure 20. Ask the same thing in different words and two-thirds of the sources change.** “Is Target open on Easter” and “Target Easter hours,” asked the same day, shared about 35% of cited sources on average. The verdict stayed the same; the sources rotated. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/ai-answer-source-overlap-by-wording.png)

| Comparison | Average shared sources | Pairs |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Same local query, another day | 61% | 18 pairs |
| Same brand, same day, different wording | 35% | 157 pairs |

**Figure 21. Local AI answers were more faithful to their sources than average.** 87.8% of 2,253 local claims were supported by the cited pages, versus 84.5% of 95,767 other claims. Faithful to sources is not the same as accurate for your location. Across the 46 chains asked about on Easter, the open-or-closed verdict never contradicted itself; every apparent conflict our tagger flagged turned out, when read by hand, to be phrasing like “Yes, it’s closed.” Local answers were also more faithful to their sources than average (7.3% unsupported claims vs 11.1%). But faithful to sources is not the same as accurate for your location, and the sources rotate.

![Diagram of an owner-confirmed Local AI Registry record feeding the business website, Google Business Profile, directories and press, so AI answers match](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

**Illustration 6. One confirmed record, pushed everywhere AI looks.** Because AI rotates between sources, a business’s facts need to match on its website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. Local AI Registry starts from one owner-confirmed record. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/local-answer-gap/images/single-source-of-truth-for-ai-local-aeo-illustration.png)

AEO takeaway

Sources rotate, so your facts have to match everywhere.

### What to do

Make your hours, address, services and prices identical on your website, Google Business Profile, directories and press. When the AI swaps one source for another, the answer should not change.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Directory submissions and listing management keep every source in agreement with the owner-confirmed Local AI Registry record, the single source of truth.

## Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization company built for local businesses. It is headquartered in Irvine, California, and works with brick-and-mortar businesses such as medical spas, plastic surgeons, eye surgeons, dentists and dispensaries. Its local AEO services follow the playbook above:

- **Free business record.** A public, owner-claimable record of what AI says about the business, with every fact confirmed by the owner.
- **AI visibility audit.** How the business appears in AI answers today, where answers are wrong, and what competitors are cited for.
- **Google Business Profile management.** Location-level hours, holiday hours, services and updates kept current.
- **Press releases and media.** Earned coverage in the news sources AI cites most for local questions.
- **AEO content.** Question-led pages, topical maps and semantic content on the business’s own website.
- **Technical AEO.** LocalBusiness schema, llms.txt, readable pages and AI-readable media.
- **Listing consistency.** Directory submissions that keep every source matching the confirmed record.

Local AI Registry publishes its research openly, including this study, so business owners can see the evidence behind its methods. Business owners can [claim their record for free at localairegistry.com](https://localairegistry.com) and see what AI says about them today.

## Frequently asked questions

### What is answer engine optimization (AEO)?

Answer engine optimization (AEO) is the practice of making a business’s facts clear, consistent and readable so AI systems such as Google AI Overviews, ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot include the business accurately in the answers they write. SEO earns a place in a list of links; AEO earns a place inside the answer.

### What is the difference between AEO and GEO?

Generative engine optimization (GEO) and answer engine optimization (AEO) describe the same goal: being cited and described correctly in AI-generated answers. GEO is the term used in academic research; AEO is more common in marketing. For local businesses, both come down to accurate, consistent, machine-readable facts in the sources AI reads.

### Where does Google’s AI get information about local businesses?

In Local AI Registry’s analysis of 207 Google AI Overviews about local businesses, news outlets supplied 67.5% of citations. Gannett newspapers alone were cited in 90.3% of answers. The businesses’ own websites supplied 6.5% of citations, and directories such as Yelp and MapQuest supplied 0.5%.

### Does ranking on Google mean AI will cite my website?

Not necessarily. Brand websites ranked on Google’s first page in 147 of 157 brand questions, but the AI cited them in 70. Ranking is close to a requirement (only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside page one), but it does not guarantee the AI will use the page.

### Why does Google’s AI tell people to check with their local store?

Because it usually lacks location-level facts. 83.6% of local AI answers in the study told people to check locally or call ahead, 65.7% described the whole chain instead of one location, and only 1 of 207 gave a street address or phone number.

### How can a local business get into AI answers?

Based on this research: see what AI says about the business today; earn coverage in sources AI already cites, such as local news; publish location-level facts in plain text and structured data; answer real customer questions on the business’s own site; keep facts identical everywhere; and make sure key pages are readable without scripts.

### Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) provides answer engine optimization (AEO) and generative engine optimization (GEO) services for local businesses. It builds a verified public record for each business, has the owner confirm it, and pushes those facts to the places AI reads through Google Business Profile management, press releases, structured data, AEO content and listing consistency. It also runs a dedicated local AI research team, which produced this study.

### What is Local AI Registry?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization (AEO) company for local businesses, headquartered in Irvine, California. It keeps a verified, owner-confirmed public record of each business and pushes those facts to the sources that ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot read. Its dedicated research team publishes original studies on how AI answers local questions, including The Local Answer Gap.

### How do I get my business recommended by ChatGPT, Claude or Gemini?

AI assistants recommend businesses whose facts they can find, read and confirm across several sources. This research points to six steps: check what AI says about you now, earn coverage in sources AI already cites such as local news, publish location-level facts in plain text and LocalBusiness schema, answer real customer questions on your own site, keep your facts identical everywhere, and make key pages readable without scripts. Local AI Registry offers a free business record and AI visibility audit as the starting point.

### How does a local business show up in Google AI Overviews?

Rank on Google’s first page and give the AI something quotable. In Local AI Registry’s study, only 4.1% of business-site citations came from outside page one, but ranking alone was not enough: brand sites ranked in 147 of 157 brand questions and were cited in 70. Pages that answer one question clearly in the first sentence, with the location’s own facts, give the AI something to cite.

### Does Google Business Profile affect what AI says about my business?

Very likely. In this study, 51.6% of claims the AI attributed to a store locator or official site were not supported by any page it cited, which suggests Google’s AI draws store-level facts such as hours from a source it does not cite, likely Google’s own business listing data. Keeping your Google Business Profile complete and current is the safest way to make sure those facts are right.

### Is AEO replacing SEO?

No. AEO builds on SEO. Google’s AI rarely cited business pages that did not already rank on page one, so SEO remains the entry ticket. AEO adds what ranking alone does not: clear, consistent, machine-readable facts, and coverage in the third-party sources AI trusts.

### What should a local business look for in an AEO company?

Look for a company that shows you what AI says about your business today, measures visibility as a rate across many AI answers instead of a single screenshot, fixes location-level facts at the source, earns coverage in the publications AI cites, and reports its work in a way you can verify. Local AI Registry is built around these principles, with owner-confirmed records, public track records and no long-term contracts.

### Is this research based on real AI answers?

Yes. It re-analyzes the public records from Xu, Iqbal and Montgomery’s IMC 2026 study of Google AI Overviews: 55,393 searches, 7,583 AI Overview answers and 98,020 fact-checked claims, collected in the United States between March 13 and April 21, 2026. The dataset is licensed CC BY 4.0.

## Limits of this research

- The local questions are mostly national chains on one holiday; 185 of 271 local searches were collected on April 6, 2026, the day after Easter. Independent businesses are not in the data.
- One engine: Google AI Overviews. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Microsoft Copilot and Google AI Mode may behave differently.
- Claim verdicts come from the original study’s AI judge (Grok 4.1), which its authors audited. We reused their verdicts and did not re-judge.
- Source groups, the local filter and the control levels in the priority map are Local AI Registry’s own rules and judgment. Some counts are small (31 first-party claims, 18 repeat-query pairs), so read those as signals, not settled rates.
- The playbook applies chain-level findings to independent businesses. That is our reasoning from the data, not something the data measured directly.

4. Liu, N. F., Zhang, T., and Liang, P. (2023). [Evaluating Verifiability in Generative Search Engines](https://arxiv.org/abs/2304.09848). *Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2023*.

# Med Spa Search Signals: what Google searches reveal about aesthetic clients and sales

  

By the [Local AI Registry Research Team](#authors)
  

The short answer
  

Local AI Registry’s analysis of five years of Google searches shows that a big brand with the same shopper can read a small brand’s sales early. Growth in Sephora searches tracked growth in Jeuveau maker Evolus’s revenue at 0.71 over 15 quarters, while Jeuveau’s own searches scored −0.08. Using Sephora, we estimate Evolus’s Q4 2026 revenue at about $107 million, above the $95 million to $102 million implied by guidance. The same data shows med spa clients live on the Pilates map, men search for surgery but not upkeep, and January to March is research season.
  

- **94** searches tested as stand-ins
- **15** quarters of company sales
- **49** states compared
- **680** search pairs tested
- **41** charts, maps, explainers and 3D visuals

## Key findings

- Local AI Registry found that growth in U.S. Google searches for Sephora tracked growth in Evolus revenue (the maker of Jeuveau) at 0.71 across 15 quarters, while searches for Jeuveau itself scored −0.08.
- Sephora averages about 6.1 million U.S. Google searches a month and Jeuveau about 18,100, so Sephora’s search trend is 338 times larger to read, Local AI Registry found.
- Using last quarter’s growth plus Sephora searches, Local AI Registry’s estimate landed within 7% of Evolus revenue in 11 of 14 quarters and puts Q4 2026 revenue at about $107M, above the $95M to $102M implied by company guidance.
- Equinox searches moved opposite to Jeuveau sales over five years (−0.78) but showed no link quarter to quarter (0.02), so a long-trend match alone can mislead, according to Local AI Registry.
- In 2025, searches for “botox” rose 10% to 16% year over year while Botox Cosmetic sales fell 5% to 12%, which shows “botox” works as a category word, Local AI Registry found.
- Club Pilates brand searches fell 17% year over year in Q3 2026 while Pilates searches were still up 17% in Q2 2026, and Xponential reported same-store sales down 7.5%, according to Local AI Registry.
- Across 49 states, Local AI Registry found that searches for med spa treatments follow the same state ranking as Pilates (0.81), Tesla and Rolex (0.75), and run opposite to crockpots and fishing licenses (−0.66).
- Men make up about 46% of searches for liposuction, facelifts and nose jobs but 22% to 33% of searches for Botox, nails, lashes and spray tans, Local AI Registry found.
- Local AI Registry found that Botox searches hold near their yearly average in January to March (102) while Botox sales to clinics run 8% below it (92).
- Of 680 pairs of beauty and everyday searches, only 2 matched on timing, states and age mix, and only 1 of 14 viral “search twin” pairs held up, according to Local AI Registry.

## What is a search signal, and why borrow one from a bigger brand?

A search signal is a trend in how often people search for something on Google. When searches for a product rise, sales often follow. The problem is that many brands are searched too rarely to read. Jeuveau, the wrinkle-relaxing injection made by Evolus, averages about 18,100 U.S. searches a month. Sephora averages about 6.1 million.

So we borrowed the signal. We looked for a much bigger search that shares Jeuveau’s customer and moves with Evolus’s sales. Then we used it to estimate a quarter Evolus has not reported yet. Along the way, we used the same data to describe who the med spa client is, where they live, when they research and what else they buy.

![Two panels: Jeuveau with 18,100 monthly searches and a noisy bar pattern; Sephora with 6.1 million searches and a steady rising pattern, arrow pointing to an estimate of Jeuveau sales](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.png)

**Illustration 1. Borrow the search signal of a bigger brand with the same shopper.** A niche brand's searches bounce too much to read. A big brand with the same shopper gives a steadier signal to estimate from. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/borrow-a-bigger-search-signal-illustration.png)

![Animation: two coin-flip lines draw across; with a handful of flips the share of heads jumps wildly, with thousands of flips it settles near 50 percent](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-more-searches-are-steadier-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 1. Why more searches give a steadier signal.** Flip a coin ten times and you might get seven heads. Flip it thousands of times and you get very close to half. Search data behaves the same way, which is why a brand with millions of searches is easier to read than one with thousands. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-more-searches-are-steadier-explainer.svg)

![Bar chart of average monthly U.S. Google searches: Sephora 6,120,000, Equinox 368,000, Botox 165,000, Jeuveau 18,100](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.png)

**Figure 1. Sephora gets 338 times more Google searches than Jeuveau.** Jeuveau averages about 18,100 U.S. searches a month. Sephora averages 6.1 million, so its search trend is far steadier to read. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/monthly-google-searches-sephora-vs-jeuveau.png)

### Terms used in this study

Search signal

A trend in how often people search for something on Google, used as an early read on what they will buy.

Proxy search

A search for a bigger brand or topic with the same customers, used when the brand you care about gets too few searches to read.

Nowcast

An estimate of a period that has already started but has not been reported yet, such as a quarter's sales before the earnings release.

Year-over-year growth

The change against the same period a year earlier, which removes normal seasonal ups and downs.

Correlation

A number from −1 to 1 that shows how closely two series move together. It shows a match, not a cause.

Category word

A word people use for a whole type of product, the way “botox” is used for any wrinkle-relaxing injection.

Search twin

Two unrelated searches whose charts move together. We test them on timing, states and age mix to see if the same people are behind them.

Answer engine optimization (AEO)

Making a business’s facts clear, consistent and machine-readable so AI systems such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Google AI Overviews include it accurately.

## Has anyone used other brands' searches to estimate aesthetics sales?

Using Google searches to read the economy early is an established idea. Hal Varian and Hyunyoung Choi showed in 2012 that Google Trends data improves near-term estimates of retail sales, car sales and travel. Sharad Goel and colleagues showed in 2010 that searches anticipate box office, game and music sales.

Those studies use searches for the product itself. We could not find published work that estimates aesthetic injectable sales from another brand’s searches, or that tests the med spa client against everyday searches on timing, states and age at once. That is the gap this study fills.

## How we did this research

- Search data: weekly U.S. Google Trends interest for 101 searches from November 2021 to November 2026, each pulled on its own scale, via DataForSEO. 94 had five full years of usable data and were tested as stand-ins.
- Search volume: average monthly U.S. Google searches from Google Ads, November 2025 to October 2026, via DataForSEO.
- Sales: Evolus total net revenue for each quarter from Q1 2022 to Q3 2026 and its 2026 guidance of $330 million to $337 million; AbbVie global Botox Cosmetic net revenue from Q1 2023 to Q3 2026 (Q4 2023 and Q4 2024 are the full year minus the first three quarters); Xponential Fitness results for Q3 2025 to Q3 2026.
- Stand-in test: for each search, we compared growth against the same quarter a year before with Evolus’s revenue growth (15 quarters), then compared the quarter-to-quarter changes in those growth rates. A useful stand-in has to pass both.
- Estimate: Evolus revenue growth predicted from last quarter’s growth and Sephora search growth, tested by hiding one quarter at a time. The Q4 2026 estimate uses Sephora searches from October 4 to November 14, 2026, against the same weeks of 2025.
- States: Google Trends state interest over the past five years for 49 states (Wyoming and Washington, D.C. left out because of small samples). The med spa score averages eight treatment searches after putting each on the same scale. Matches are rank correlations.
- People: DataForSEO’s search panel age and gender mix for 59 searches over the past 12 months, and BLS Consumer Expenditure Survey 2024 personal care spending by age.
- Search twins: 17 beauty searches against 40 everyday searches (680 pairs), tested on timing (monthly match of 0.50 or more, with and without long trends), states (rank match of 0.35 or more) and age mix (85% overlap or more).
- All aggregated tables are in the [CSV download](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/data/med-spa-search-signals-data.csv).

![Animation: two years of quarterly bars with a big holiday quarter; first a dashed coral arrow compares last year's holiday quarter with this January and wrongly suggests a drop, then a blue arrow compares January with last January and shows real growth](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-compare-same-time-last-year-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 2. Why we compare with the same time last year.** Most businesses have busy and slow seasons. Comparing January with December makes any business look like it is shrinking. Comparing January with last January removes the season and shows real change. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/why-compare-same-time-last-year-explainer.svg)

## Can Sephora searches predict Jeuveau sales?

Yes, better than Jeuveau’s own searches. Sephora search growth matched Evolus revenue growth at 0.71 over 15 quarters; Jeuveau searches scored −0.08.

![Line chart of year-over-year growth by quarter, Q1 2023 to Q3 2026: Sephora searches and Evolus revenue move together, correlation 0.71](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/sephora-search-growth-vs-jeuveau-evolus-revenue-growth.png)

**Figure 2. Sephora search growth tracks Jeuveau sales growth at 0.71.** Across 15 quarters, Sephora search growth and Evolus revenue growth line up at 0.71. Both slowed through 2024 and both rose in Q2 2026. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/sephora-search-growth-vs-jeuveau-evolus-revenue-growth.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/sephora-search-growth-vs-jeuveau-evolus-revenue-growth.png)

![Animation: two lines; the second line changes from moving randomly (0, no link) to mostly following the first (0.7, a strong link) to matching it exactly (1.0, a perfect link)](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-a-match-number-means-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 3. What does a “0.71 match” mean?** A match number (a correlation) runs from 0 to 1. Near 0, two things move separately; near 1, they rise and fall together. A minus sign means they move in opposite directions. It shows a link, not a cause. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-a-match-number-means-explainer.svg)

We tested 94 searches, from Sephora and Ulta to Equinox, Pilates, Wingstop and Taylor Swift. Three passed both tests: Sephora, espresso martini and Taylor Swift. Testing this many searches means some will match by luck, so we only use a stand-in with a real link to the same shopper. Of the three, only Sephora has one.

![Heatmap of 12 searches scored on two tests against Evolus revenue growth; Sephora 0.71 and 0.46, Equinox -0.78 and 0.02](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/which-searches-predict-jeuveau-sales-heatmap.png)

**Figure 3. Only three searches match Jeuveau sales on both the trend and the changes.** A useful stand-in has to pass both tests. Sephora, Taylor Swift and espresso martini pass both; Sephora is the only one that shares the beauty shopper. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/which-searches-predict-jeuveau-sales-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/which-searches-predict-jeuveau-sales-heatmap.png)

![Two by two scatter of 94 searches by long-trend match and quarter-to-quarter match with Evolus revenue; Sephora in the real signal corner, Equinox in trend only](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-proxy-test-2x2-trend-vs-quarterly-match.png)

**Figure 4. Of 94 searches, few track Jeuveau sales for real.** Most searches fall near the middle. Equinox sits in the trend-only corner: strong over five years, no link quarter to quarter. Sephora sits in the real-signal corner. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-proxy-test-2x2-trend-vs-quarterly-match.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-proxy-test-2x2-trend-vs-quarterly-match.png)

![Interactive 3D orbit of 94 searches around a central Jeuveau sales node; closer means a better long-trend match and higher means a better quarter-to-quarter match; Sephora, Taylor Swift and espresso martini sit high and close in coral](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/jeuveau-proxy-search-orbit-3d-poster.png)

**Interactive 2. Explore all 94 stand-in searches orbiting Jeuveau sales in 3D.** Distance from the center shows how well each search matches Jeuveau sales on the long trend; height shows how well it matches the quarter-to-quarter changes. Only the coral searches, linked to the center, pass both. Equinox and Planet Fitness sit in dark ink: trend only. Drag to turn, scroll to zoom, hover a ball for its numbers. [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/jeuveau-proxy-search-orbit-3d-poster.png) · [Data](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/data/med-spa-search-signals-data.csv)

![Two panels: left, two lines drifting in opposite directions labeled trend only (Equinox); right, two lines rising and falling together labeled real signal (Sephora)](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/trend-match-vs-real-signal-illustration.png)

**Illustration 2. A real signal matches the ups and downs, not just the long trend.** Two series can look related over five years just because both drift. A real signal also matches the quarter-to-quarter changes. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/trend-match-vs-real-signal-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/trend-match-vs-real-signal-illustration.png)

Equinox is the trap. Over five years its searches move opposite to Jeuveau sales (−0.78), which looks like a gym-versus-injectables budget fight. Quarter to quarter there is no link (0.02). The match came from two slow trends pointing different ways. “Equinox” is also a car and a season, which muddies its searches further.

AEO takeaway

A big brand with the same customer can be a better gauge than your own brand name.

### What to do

If your brand or category is too small to read in search, find a large search that shares your customer, and check it against your own sales before you rely on it.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry publishes this research openly and its AI visibility audit shows how often a business is named when people ask AI about its category.

## What do searches say about Jeuveau's Q4 2026 sales?

They point above guidance. Our estimate for Evolus’s Q4 2026 revenue is about $107 million; the company’s guidance implies $95 million to $102 million.

![Line chart of Evolus quarterly revenue and our leave-one-out estimate, Q1 2023 to Q3 2026, plus a Q4 2026 estimate of $107M against a guidance-implied range of $95M to $102M](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/evolus-jeuveau-q4-2026-revenue-estimate-vs-guidance.png)

**Figure 5. Our search estimate puts Evolus Q4 2026 revenue at $107M, above guidance.** Tested by hiding one quarter at a time, the estimate landed within 7% of actual revenue in 11 of 14 quarters. For Q4 2026 it points to about $107M; guidance implies $95M to $102M. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/evolus-jeuveau-q4-2026-revenue-estimate-vs-guidance.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/evolus-jeuveau-q4-2026-revenue-estimate-vs-guidance.png)

![Animation: a timeline from October to February; weekly search dots appear through the October to December quarter, a coral marker for our early read appears in mid-November, and the company's report flag lights up in January](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-a-nowcast-is-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 4. What is a “nowcast”?** Companies report a quarter weeks after it ends. Search data arrives every week, so it can give a read on the quarter while it is still happening. That early read is called a nowcast. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-a-nowcast-is-explainer.svg)

Sephora searches from October 4 to November 14, 2026, are up 7.5% on the same weeks of 2025. With last quarter’s growth of 13.1%, that points to Q4 revenue up about 18%, roughly $101 million to $113 million. Evolus guided to $330 million to $337 million for 2026 and has reported $235.2 million through Q3.

![Bar chart of average forecast miss in points of growth: both inputs 6.6, Sephora only 8.6, last quarter only 9.2, same as last quarter 9.2](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/adding-sephora-search-cuts-jeuveau-forecast-error.png)

**Figure 6. Adding Sephora searches cut the average miss from 9.2 to 6.6 points.** Each quarter was predicted with that quarter hidden. Using last quarter's growth plus Sephora searches missed by 6.6 points of growth on average, against 9.2 without Sephora. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/adding-sephora-search-cuts-jeuveau-forecast-error.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/adding-sephora-search-cuts-jeuveau-forecast-error.png)

![Waffle of 14 quarters: 11 estimates within 7% of Evolus revenue, 3 further off](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/jeuveau-revenue-estimate-accuracy-waffle.png)

**Figure 7. The estimate landed within 7% of actual sales in 11 of 14 quarters.** In a hide-one-quarter test from Q2 2023 to Q3 2026, the estimate was within 7% of reported revenue in 11 of 14 quarters. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/jeuveau-revenue-estimate-accuracy-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/jeuveau-revenue-estimate-accuracy-waffle.png)

Search moved in the same quarter as sales in our tests, not a quarter ahead. So this is an early read, available about seven weeks before Evolus last shared preliminary Q4 numbers (January 9, 2026). It is research, not investment advice.

AEO takeaway

Search gives an early read on a quarter before the books close.

### What to do

Compare searches for your business and your category with the same weeks last year. A clear gap is an early warning or an early win.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s Google Business Profile management keeps the profile people find by name current, and its AI visibility audit shows how the business appears in AI answers today.

## Do searches for a brand track that brand's sales?

For brand names, yes. For category words, no. “botox” rose in 2025 while Botox Cosmetic sales fell; Jeuveau searches matched Evolus’s sales direction in 10 of 11 quarters.

![Diagram: the search word botox sits above three toxin brands, Botox, Jeuveau and Dysport](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-category-word-vs-brand-names-illustration.png)

**Illustration 3. “Botox” works like Kleenex: one word for a whole category.** People search “botox” for any neurotoxin treatment, so the word tracks demand for the whole category. Brand names like Jeuveau track the brand. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-category-word-vs-brand-names-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-category-word-vs-brand-names-illustration.png)

![Line chart indexed to Q1 2023 = 100: botox searches rise in 2025 while AbbVie Botox Cosmetic sales fall; correlation 0.13](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searches-vs-botox-cosmetic-sales.png)

**Figure 8. “Botox” searches rose in 2025 while Botox Cosmetic sales fell.** In 2025, “botox” searches ran 10% to 16% above the year before while global Botox Cosmetic sales ran 5% to 12% below. Over 15 quarters the two barely relate (0.13). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searches-vs-botox-cosmetic-sales.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searches-vs-botox-cosmetic-sales.png)

![Heatmap of year-over-year change by quarter, 2024 to 2026: botox searches up while Botox sales fall in 2025; jeuveau searches and Evolus revenue rise together](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/brand-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-heatmap.png)

**Figure 9. Jeuveau searches moved with Jeuveau sales in 10 of 11 quarters; “botox” did not.** Blue is growth and coral is decline against the same quarter a year before. The brand name Jeuveau matched its maker's sales direction in 10 of 11 quarters; the everyday word “botox” did not track the Botox brand. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/brand-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/brand-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-heatmap.png)

Club Pilates shows the same rule from the other side. Brand searches grew 15% in Q1 2025, stalled by mid-2025 and fell 17% by Q3 2026. Xponential’s North America same-store sales turned negative in Q3 2025 (down 1%) and kept falling, to down 7.5% in Q3 2026 (Club Pilates down 5.6%). Plain “pilates” searches were still up 17% in Q2 2026. The category grew; the brand did not.

![Line chart indexed to Q1 2023 = 100: pilates searches keep rising into 2026 while club pilates searches fall after early 2025](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/club-pilates-brand-search-vs-pilates-category-search.png)

**Figure 10. Club Pilates searches fell 17% while Pilates searches kept growing.** Club Pilates brand searches were down 17% year over year in Q3 2026. That quarter Xponential reported same-store sales down 7.5% across its brands and 5.6% at Club Pilates. Plain “pilates” searches were still up 17% in Q2 2026. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/club-pilates-brand-search-vs-pilates-category-search.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/club-pilates-brand-search-vs-pilates-category-search.png)

AEO takeaway

Your name is the number to watch, next to your category.

### What to do

Track searches for your business name against searches for what you sell. If your name falls while the category holds, a competitor is taking share.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s AI visibility audit shows which competitors AI names for your category, and its listing consistency work keeps your name the same everywhere AI looks.

## Where do med spa clients live?

In the same states that search for Pilates. Our combined med spa score matches Pilates search by state at 0.81.

![Animation: eight states ranked by med spa searches on the left are joined by lines to the same states ranked by Pilates searches, with lines running mostly straight; then the right column switches to Equinox and the lines cross](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/how-a-state-by-state-match-works-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 5. How a state-by-state match works.** Rank every state by one search, then by another, and connect each state. If the lines run straight across, the two searches are big in the same places. Shown here with eight of the 49 states. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/how-a-state-by-state-match-works-explainer.svg)

![Two by two scatter of 49 states: med spa search score against Pilates search interest, rank match 0.81; Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California top right](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-vs-pilates-search-by-state-2x2.png)

**Figure 11. States that search for med spas also search for Pilates (0.81).** We combined eight treatment searches into one score per state. Its ranking matches Pilates at 0.81. Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California lead; Vermont, South Dakota, Iowa and West Virginia trail. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-vs-pilates-search-by-state-2x2.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-vs-pilates-search-by-state-2x2.png)

![Heatmap of state rank matches with the med spa search score: Pilates 0.81, Love Island, Tesla and Rolex 0.75, Uber Eats 0.74; crockpot and fishing license -0.66](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/everyday-searches-that-share-the-med-spa-state-map.png)

**Figure 12. The med spa map looks like Pilates, Tesla and Rolex, not crockpots.** Across 49 states, the med spa search map matches Pilates, Tesla, Rolex, Love Island and Uber Eats. It runs opposite to crockpots, fishing licenses, puppies and air fryers. Much of this is the map of city life and income. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/everyday-searches-that-share-the-med-spa-state-map.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/everyday-searches-that-share-the-med-spa-state-map.png)

![Map of the United States with concentric rings over each state sized by its med spa search score; the largest rings sit over Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-heat-map-concentric-rings-by-state.png)

**Figure 13. Med spa searches run hottest in Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California.** Each state's rings grow with its combined score across eight treatment searches (Botox near me, lip filler, microneedling, HydraFacial, med spa near me, laser hair removal, chemical peel, dermaplaning). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-heat-map-concentric-rings-by-state.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-search-heat-map-concentric-rings-by-state.png)
