**Figure 14. Med spa states are Pilates states (0.81 match).** Coral dots show med spa searches; blue rings show Pilates searches. Where one is big, the other usually is too: the state rankings match at 0.81. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-pilates-search-concentric-ring-map.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-pilates-search-concentric-ring-map.png)

![Map with a coral dot for each state's med spa search score inside an ink ring for Sephora search interest; rank match 0.74](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-sephora-search-concentric-ring-map.png)

**Figure 15. Med spa states are also Sephora states (0.74 match).** The same shopper shows up in place as well as in time. States that search most for med spa treatments also search most for Sephora (rank match 0.74). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-sephora-search-concentric-ring-map.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-sephora-search-concentric-ring-map.png)

![Map with a coral dot for each state's med spa search score inside a gray ring for Equinox search interest; big rings sit around small dots, rank match −0.54](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-equinox-search-concentric-ring-map.png)

**Figure 16. Med spa states are not Equinox states (−0.54).** Equinox fails on place too. Its searches are biggest in different states from med spa searches (rank match −0.54). Equinox is also a car, which spreads its searches. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-equinox-search-concentric-ring-map.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-vs-equinox-search-concentric-ring-map.png)

![Interactive 3D network of 52 searches arranged around a central med spa map node; treatments, Pilates, Tesla, Rolex and Sephora sit close in coral, while crockpot, fishing license and Monster Energy sit far out in dark ink](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-state-map-3d-network-poster.png)

**Interactive 1. Explore 52 searches in 3D: the closer to the center, the more a search shares the med spa state map.** Each ball is a search. Its distance from the center shows how closely its state ranking matches the med spa map; coral is 0.6 or more, blue 0.3 to 0.6, gray and ink are weak or opposite. Lines join searches whose state maps match at 0.62 or more. Drag to turn, scroll to zoom, hover a ball for its number. [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-state-map-3d-network-poster.png) · [Data](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/data/med-spa-search-signals-data.csv)

Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California lead the med spa score; Vermont, South Dakota, Iowa and West Virginia trail. The everyday searches that share the map (Pilates, Tesla, Rolex, Uber Eats, sushi) and the ones that oppose it (crockpots, fishing licenses, air fryers) suggest much of this is the map of city life and income. Treat it as a wallet signal, not a cause.

The ring maps put two searches on one map. Med spa states are Pilates states (0.81) and Sephora states (0.74), but not Equinox states (−0.54). So Sephora passes on place as well as on time, and Equinox fails on both.

AEO takeaway

Med spa demand is concentrated, and it sits next to fitness and luxury spending.

### What to do

Put more budget in the states and cities where your treatment and your partners are searched most.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s listing consistency work and location pages make each location easy for AI to find in the markets where it operates.

## Who searches for aesthetic treatments?

Men search for surgery about as often as for anything else (46%) but rarely for upkeep (22% to 33%). Lip filler searchers are about 33; Botox searchers about 41.

![Bar chart of men's share of searches: liposuction, facelift and nose job 46%, Botox 33%, nail salon and lash extensions 28%, spray tan 22%](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/share-of-aesthetic-searches-by-men.png)

**Figure 17. Men make up 46% of surgery searches but 22% to 33% of upkeep searches.** Men's share of liposuction, facelift and nose job searches (46%) is close to their 44% median share of everyday searches. For upkeep it drops to 22% to 33%. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/share-of-aesthetic-searches-by-men.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/share-of-aesthetic-searches-by-men.png)

![Heatmap of each treatment's searches by age band; lip filler and Brazilian wax heaviest at 18 to 34, Botox and nail salon heaviest at 55 to 64](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/who-searches-each-aesthetic-treatment-by-age-heatmap.png)

**Figure 18. Lip filler searchers skew young; Botox and nail searches skew older.** Each row adds to 100%. The typical lip filler searcher is about 33 and the typical Botox searcher about 41. Age bands come from a search panel, so read them as relative, not exact. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/who-searches-each-aesthetic-treatment-by-age-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/who-searches-each-aesthetic-treatment-by-age-heatmap.png)

![Bar chart of 2024 personal care spending per household by age: under 25 $647, 25 to 34 $863, 35 to 44 $1,202, 45 to 54 $1,226, 55 to 64 $1,023](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/personal-care-spending-by-age-2024.png)

**Figure 19. Households aged 35 to 54 spend the most on personal care, about $1,200 a year.** The youngest treatment searchers sit in the households that spend least on personal care. Households under 35 spend $647 to $863 a year; households 35 to 54 spend about $1,200. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/personal-care-spending-by-age-2024.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/personal-care-spending-by-age-2024.png)

The youngest treatment searchers sit in the households that spend least on personal care: $647 a year under 25 and $863 at 25 to 34, against about $1,200 at 35 to 54. In a 2026 Zenoti survey, 26% of Gen Z had delayed medical or dental care to pay for beauty, against 11% of boomers. For younger treatments, payment plans and memberships matter most.

AEO takeaway

Different treatments draw different people.

### What to do

Write for the real searcher: surgery pages for men as well as women, and clear prices and payment options for the youngest treatments.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s AEO content answers the questions each audience asks, on the business’s own website.

## When do clients research, and when do they buy?

Clients research all year, including January to March. Botox searches hold at 102 in Q1 while Botox sales to clinics drop to 92.

![Timeline of four quarters: January to March searching, April to June booking, July to September quieter, October to December holiday push](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/aesthetics-research-season-q1-illustration.png)

**Illustration 5. January to March is when clients research; spring is when they book.** Botox searches stay near their yearly average in Q1 while sales to practices run 8% below it, then rise in Q2. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/aesthetics-research-season-q1-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/aesthetics-research-season-q1-illustration.png)

![Grouped bar chart of each quarter against the year's average, 2023 to 2025: searches 102, 101, 97, 101; Botox Cosmetic sales 92, 105, 96, 106](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-seasonality.png)

**Figure 20. In January to March, Botox searches hold at 102 while sales to clinics drop to 92.** 100 is the year's average. Searches barely change by season, but AbbVie's Botox sales to practices run 8% below average in Q1 and 5% to 6% above in Q2 and Q4. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-seasonality.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-search-vs-sales-by-quarter-seasonality.png)

These are AbbVie’s sales to practices, not what patients pay, so clinics stocking up in Q4 explains part of the Q1 dip. Even so, searches do not take a break after the holidays.

AEO takeaway

Going quiet in January means going quiet while people decide.

### What to do

Keep marketing in January to March, when searches hold steady and competitors pull back.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s press releases and AEO content can be timed to when people search, not when budgets reset.

## What else do aesthetic clients spend on?

Dining out, clothing, nails and spas, in that order of what they would cut first. Treatments come last: 24% would cut them.

![Bar chart of the share of aesthetic clients who would cut each category: dining 54%, clothing 43%, nail care 42%, spa or massage 40%, travel 31%, fitness 27%, aesthetic treatments 24%](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-aesthetic-clients-would-cut-first.png)

**Figure 21. Aesthetic clients would cut dining out (54%) long before treatments (24%).** Asked where they would cut spending, aesthetic clients put treatments last. The categories above it are where the same budget goes today. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-aesthetic-clients-would-cut-first.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/what-aesthetic-clients-would-cut-first.png)

![Heatmap of everyday search categories against botox near me: dating and weddings pass 1.5 of 3 tests on average, drinks have the best state match at 0.36, weight-loss drugs 0.08](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searchers-best-partner-categories-heatmap.png)

**Figure 22. Wedding and dating searches share the most with Botox searchers.** For “botox near me”, we averaged each category's state match, age-mix overlap and tests passed. Dating and wedding searches pass the most tests; drinks match best on states; weight-loss drugs share the age mix but not the states. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searchers-best-partner-categories-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-searchers-best-partner-categories-heatmap.png)

![Two by two of everyday categories by state match and age-mix overlap with botox near me; dating and weddings, drinks and fitness in the partner-now corner, weight-loss drugs low on state match](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-co-marketing-partner-priority-2x2.png)

**Figure 23. Partner priority map: who shares Botox searchers' places and age.** Bubble size is tests passed. Dating and weddings, fitness and drinks sit in the partner-now corner. Fitness is also one of the last things clients cut (27%), while dining out is the first (54%). [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-co-marketing-partner-priority-2x2.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/med-spa-co-marketing-partner-priority-2x2.png)

Card-level spending data on med spa clients is not public. These public sources point the same way: wedding, dating and fitness businesses share the most with Botox searchers. Wine matches best on states, but it falls under dining out, the first thing clients cut. Weight-loss drug searches share the age mix but not the states. In a 2026 Morning Consult survey for LaserAway, 53% of U.S. adults said they would give up everyday spending to afford non-surgical treatments.

AEO takeaway

The best partners share your client and survive budget cuts.

### What to do

Start with bridal shops and Pilates or fitness studios. Test drinks or dining with a one-off event before a standing deal.

### How Local AI Registry does it

Local AI Registry’s press releases and media service can announce joint offers in the sources AI reads.

## Which search twins share a real audience?

Very few. Of 680 beauty and everyday search pairs, 2 matched on timing, states and age mix: nose job with tarot, and Botox with wedding dress. Of our 14 viral pairs, only nose job and tarot held up.

![Three boxes: time, do searches rise and fall together; place, are they big in the same states; people, same age and gender mix](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/three-tests-for-search-twins-illustration.png)

**Illustration 4. Three tests decide whether two searches share an audience.** A five-year chart match is only the first test. Pairs that also match on states and on the age and gender of searchers point to the same people. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/three-tests-for-search-twins-illustration.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/three-tests-for-search-twins-illustration.png)

![Animation: summer pushes up both ice cream sales and sunburns; below, city life and income push up both med spa searches and Tesla searches](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/hidden-third-factor-explainer.svg)

**Explainer 6. How a hidden third factor fakes a link.** Two things can rise together because something else drives both. Ice cream and sunburns both peak in summer. Med spa and Tesla searches both run high where city life and incomes are higher. A match is a clue, not proof. [Animated SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/hidden-third-factor-explainer.svg)

![Bar chart of 680 beauty and everyday search pairs by tests passed: 2 passed all three, 49 passed two, 257 passed one, 372 passed none](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-twins-that-pass-time-place-people-tests.png)

**Figure 24. Only 2 of 680 search pairs passed all three tests.** We paired 17 beauty searches with 40 everyday searches and tested timing, states and age mix. Two pairs passed everything: nose job with tarot, and Botox with wedding dress. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-twins-that-pass-time-place-people-tests.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/search-twins-that-pass-time-place-people-tests.png)

![Waffle of 14 viral search pairs: 1 passed timing, state and age tests; 13 did not](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-correlations-that-hold-up-waffle.png)

**Figure 25. Only 1 of our 14 viral search twins held up on all three tests.** All 14 pairs in our Correlation, Not Causation posts were picked because their five-year charts matched. On states and age mix, 13 of them fell apart. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-correlations-that-hold-up-waffle.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-correlations-that-hold-up-waffle.png)

![Heatmap of 14 viral beauty and everyday search pairs scored on time, place and people; blue cells pass and beige cells fail; only nose job plus tarot is blue in all three columns](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-twins-three-test-results-heatmap.png)

**Figure 26. All 14 viral search twins, test by test: only nose job and tarot pass all three.** Blue means the pair passed that test: timing match of 0.50 or more, a state rank match of 0.35 or more that is unlikely to be chance, and age-mix overlap of 85% or more. Every pair passed on time, because that is how they were picked. Only nose job and tarot also passed on place and people. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-twins-three-test-results-heatmap.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/viral-search-twins-three-test-results-heatmap.png)

The one viral pair that held up was nose job and tarot. Across all 680 pairs, only one other passed every test: Botox with wedding dress. Here are both, test by test.

![Three small charts for Nose job and Tarot searches: five-year monthly lines that move together (0.60), a scatter of 49 states that slopes upward (+0.60), and age bars that look alike (86% overlap)](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/nose-job-and-tarot-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.png)

**Figure 27. Nose job and tarot: same timing, same states, same age mix.** Searches for nose jobs and tarot rise and fall together over five years (0.60), lead in the same states (0.60) and come from nearly the same age mix (86% overlap). It is the one viral pair that held up. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/nose-job-and-tarot-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/nose-job-and-tarot-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.png)

![Three small charts for Botox and Wedding dress searches: five-year monthly lines that move together (0.70), a scatter of 49 states that slopes upward (+0.40), and age bars that look alike (86% overlap)](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-and-wedding-dress-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.png)

**Figure 28. Botox and wedding dress: same timing, same states, same age mix.** Searches for Botox near me and wedding dresses move together (0.70), lead in the same states (0.40) and share an age mix (86% overlap). For med spas, it points to brides and bridal shops as a real audience. [SVG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-and-wedding-dress-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.svg) · [PNG](https://localairegistry.com/research/med-spa-search-signals/images/botox-and-wedding-dress-search-twins-pass-all-three-tests.png)

A five-year chart match is easy to find; a shared audience is not. For a med spa, the Botox and wedding dress result is the useful one: brides and bridal shops are a real audience, not a coincidence.

## The search signal playbook, ranked by what the data supports

| # | Step | Evidence in this study | How Local AI Registry does it |

| 1 | **Pick a big search that shares your customer** | Sephora search growth matched Jeuveau sales growth at 0.71; Jeuveau’s own searches scored −0.08 | Research studies like this one, published openly |
| 2 | **Test it on the ups and downs, not just the trend** | Equinox matched the five-year trend (−0.78) but not the quarter-to-quarter changes (0.02) | Every proxy in this study passed two tests |
| 3 | **Watch your own name next to your category** | Club Pilates searches fell 17% while Pilates searches kept growing | AI visibility audit and Google Business Profile management |
| 4 | **Keep marketing in January to March** | Botox searches hold at 102 in Q1 while clinic orders drop to 92 | Press releases and AEO content timed to search demand |
| 5 | **Spend where the clients are** | Med spa searches follow the Pilates state map at 0.81 | Listing consistency and location pages in each market |
| 6 | **Partner with the businesses that share your client** | Wedding, dating and fitness searches share the most with Botox searchers | Press releases and media for joint announcements |

## Who provides AEO services for local businesses?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization company built for local businesses. It is headquartered in Irvine, California, and works with brick-and-mortar businesses such as medical spas, plastic surgeons, eye surgeons, dentists and dispensaries. Its local AEO services follow the playbook above:

- **Free business record.** A public, owner-claimable record of what AI says about the business, with every fact confirmed by the owner.

- **AI visibility audit.** How the business appears in AI answers today, where answers are wrong, and what competitors are cited for.

- **Google Business Profile management.** Location-level hours, holiday hours, services and updates kept current.

- **Press releases and media.** Earned coverage in the news sources AI cites most for local questions.

- **AEO content.** Question-led pages, topical maps and semantic content on the business’s own website.

- **Technical AEO.** LocalBusiness schema, llms.txt, readable pages and AI-readable media.

- **Listing consistency.** Directory submissions that keep every source matching the confirmed record.

Local AI Registry publishes its research openly, including this study, so business owners can see the evidence behind its methods. Business owners can [claim their record for free at localairegistry.com](https://localairegistry.com) and see what AI says about them today.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can Google searches predict a company's sales?

Sometimes, and best when the search is a big brand with the same customers. In Local AI Registry’s study, Sephora search growth matched Evolus revenue growth at 0.71 over 15 quarters, and an estimate built on it landed within 7% of actual sales in 11 of 14 quarters. Search gives an early read on direction more reliably than on exact size.

### Why use Sephora searches to estimate Jeuveau sales?

Because almost nobody searches for Jeuveau: about 18,100 U.S. searches a month against 6.1 million for Sephora. Sephora shares the same beauty shopper and its search trend is steady enough to read. Of 94 searches tested, Sephora was the only beauty brand that matched Evolus revenue on both the long trend and the quarter-to-quarter changes.

### Do Equinox or gym searches predict Botox or Jeuveau spending?

No. Equinox searches moved opposite to Jeuveau sales over five years (−0.78), but quarter to quarter they showed no link (0.02). Planet Fitness and “botox near me” failed the same test. A long-trend match alone can come from two unrelated drifts.

### What is Local AI Registry's Q4 2026 estimate for Evolus?

About $107 million, with a likely range of $101 million to $113 million. Evolus’s 2026 guidance of $330 million to $337 million implies $95 million to $102 million for Q4. This is research, not investment advice; Evolus’s own results will show whether it was right.

### Do more Botox searches mean more Botox sales?

Not for the Botox brand. In 2025, searches for “botox” rose 10% to 16% while Botox Cosmetic sales fell 5% to 12%. People use “botox” for any wrinkle-relaxing injection, so the word tracks the whole category. Searches for the brand name Jeuveau matched its maker’s sales direction in 10 of 11 quarters.

### Which states search most for med spa treatments?

Florida, Arizona, Colorado, Utah and California lead Local AI Registry’s combined score of eight treatment searches. Vermont, South Dakota, Iowa and West Virginia trail. The same states lead searches for Pilates (0.81 match).

### Do men search for cosmetic procedures?

Yes, especially surgery. Men make up about 46% of searches for liposuction, facelifts and nose jobs, close to their 44% median share of everyday searches. For Botox, nails, lashes and spray tans, their share is 22% to 33%.

### When do people research Botox?

All year, including January to March. Botox searches stay near their yearly average in Q1 (102 against 100), while AbbVie’s Botox sales to clinics run 8% below average (92) and rise in Q2 (105).

### What do aesthetic clients cut first when money is tight?

Dining out. In NewBeauty’s 2025 survey as reported by AmSpa, 54% of aesthetic clients would cut dining out, 43% clothing and 42% nail care, while only 24% would cut aesthetic treatments.

### Which businesses should med spas partner with?

Bridal and dating-related businesses and Pilates or fitness studios. Wedding and dating searches pass the most of our timing, state and age tests with “botox near me”, and fitness shares the same states and age mix and is one of the last things clients cut.

### What is a search twin?

Two unrelated searches whose charts move together, like nose job and tarot. Of 680 pairs Local AI Registry tested, only 2 also matched on states and age mix: nose job with tarot, and Botox with wedding dress.

### What is Local AI Registry?

Local AI Registry (localairegistry.com) is an answer engine optimization (AEO) company for local businesses, headquartered in Irvine, California. It keeps a verified, owner-confirmed public record of each business and publishes original research on how people and AI find local businesses.

## Limits of this research

- Google Trends shows relative interest, not counts, and each search is scaled to its own peak. Weekly values for small searches are noisy.
- We tested 94 searches against one company’s revenue over 15 quarters. With that many tests and that few quarters, some matches are luck. Taylor Swift and espresso martini matched almost as well as Sephora.
- Evolus revenue includes its newer filler line, and AbbVie reports global Botox Cosmetic sales while we measured U.S. search.
- The Q4 2026 estimate uses about six weeks of searches and does not include the holiday weeks. It is research, not investment advice.
- Age and gender come from a search panel, not from Google, and some age bands for small searches are empty. Read them as relative.
- State matches mostly reflect where people live and how much they earn. They show shared places, not that one search causes another.
- Spending and survey figures come from the published sources named here; we did not have card-level transaction data.

## About the author

**The Local AI Registry Research Team** is Local AI Registry’s dedicated local AI research group, and its people come from some of the biggest names in search, tech and brick-and-mortar business: Google, Microsoft, Spotify, Chase, Mozilla Firefox, Allergan, Galderma, Evolus, Revance, Johnson & Johnson, Bayer, Estée Lauder, Nordstrom, Sephora, Saks Fifth Avenue, Spectrum, BitGo, Republic, NextSeed, Toptal and RxSight. It is led by a former Google Search executive, advised by a Stanford-trained dermatologist and a Northwestern professor who is a past president of the American Society for Laser Medicine and Surgery, and spread across California, Washington, Texas, New York, Florida, Brazil, Nigeria, Poland, India and Singapore. The team works from raw public data, owns and runs a local med spa, and studies how ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Google AI Overviews, Perplexity and Microsoft Copilot find and describe local businesses.

The team is a dedicated follower of the researchers who built modern AI and those who study AI search, including Geoffrey Hinton, Yoshua Bengio, Yann LeCun, Ashish Vaswani, Noam Shazeer, Demis Hassabis, Jeff Dean, Ilya Sutskever, Andrej Karpathy, Dario Amodei, Jared Kaplan, Chris Olah, Fei-Fei Li, Andrew Ng, Percy Liang, Karthik Narasimhan, Ameet Deshpande, Himabindu Lakkaraju, Aounon Kumar, Nelson F. Liu, Umar Iqbal and Jacob M. Montgomery. Their work underpins ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini, and the team studies their papers and tests their ideas against what AI says about local businesses. No affiliation or endorsement implied. See the [references](#references).

One last thing

AI is evolving every day. So is our playbook.

The engines change how they find, read and cite local businesses constantly, and what worked last quarter may not work next quarter. At Local AI Registry, our dedicated local AI research team keeps testing what works, so the businesses we serve always get the current best approach.
